1. NOTE LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: master mix is declared in a reservoir channel, not a tube
   line 35:  reservoir["A1"].load_liquid(liquid=master_mix, volume=300)
   Line 35 declares 300 ul of master mix in channel A1 of NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL (slot
     2, load name nest_12_reservoir_15ml). The request (PCR setup) puts its reagents in
     tubes, or at a temperature, and a reservoir channel is neither: 300 ul spread over the
     channel is 1.2 mm deep, open to the air and at room temperature, so it warms and
     evaporates while the run goes on, and the tip may not reach it.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Put master mix in a tube on the block (a tube rack, or a temperature module with a
     tube block), not in a reservoir channel.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html
   Source: Opentrons, thermocycler: takes the 200 ul full-skirt PCR plate
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html
   Source: ABC-Bench (Liu et al. 2026): wrong labware identifiers, the commonest LLM error
           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1
   [3f5a6e21ac39]

labware.title: master mix is declared in a reservoir channel, not a tube
labware.explanation: Line 35 declares 300 ul of master mix in channel A1 of NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL (slot 2, load name nest_12_reservoir_15ml). The request (PCR setup) puts its reagents in tubes, or at a temperature, and a reservoir channel is neither: 300 ul spread over the channel is 1.2 mm deep, open to the air and at room temperature, so it warms and evaporates while the run goes on, and the tip may not reach it.
labware.fix: Put master mix in a tube on the block (a tube rack, or a temperature module with a tube block), not in a reservoir channel.

protocol.py: 11 biology problems (9 errors, 1 warning, 1 note).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 12.5 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at
least)
   line 53:  p300_single.transfer(
   At line 53 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 12.5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul
   (this line did it 24 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the
   wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The
   simulator passes the move. Wells: well A1 in slot 2.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [e6e48ae1ff72]

2. ERROR SOURCE-TOO-SHALLOW: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 2: the liquid is
below the tip
   line 53:  p300_single.transfer(
   At line 53 the p300_single_gen2 draws 12.5 ul from master mix (well A1 in slot 2) with
   its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 188 ul, which in this
   NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.88 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and
   draws air (this line did it 15 times, after 9 times in the liquid; 188 ul of air in all).
   The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 15 wells filled from
   these draws got air instead of liquid.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Also reached 15 other wells: wells A10, A11, A12, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5 and 7 more in slot
   4.
   Fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to
   reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube
   lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.
   Source: Opentrons: liquid control (aspirates 1 mm above the bottom of the well by
   default)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/basic_commands/liquids.html
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Gilson guide to pipetting (immersion depth 2 to 3 mm for 1 to 100 ul)
           https://solutions.pipette.com/wp-content/uploads/Gilson-Guide-to-Pipetting.pdf
   Source: labautomation.io 7592: negative controls positive after aspirating air
           https://labautomation.io/t/aspiration-dispense-liquid-class-incompatibity/7592
   Source: Integra: 260 ul dead volume in a standard reservoir
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applications/minimizing-dead-volume-during-qpcr-set-divided-reservoir-assist-plus-pipetting-robot

5. ERROR CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 23 stocks
   line 86:  p300_multi.aspirate(2, batch1_sources[i])
   At line 86 the tip went into sample 2 (tube A2 in slot 3), sample 3 (tube A3 in slot 3),
   sample 4 (tube A4 in slot 3), sample 5 (tube A5 in slot 3) and 19 more while it still
   carried master mix (well A1 in slot 2), water (well A2 in slot 2), sample 1 (tube A1 in
   slot 3), sample 2 (tube A2 in slot 3) and 22 more from an earlier step (this line did it
   11 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   them then took the unwanted material along into 84 other wells: tubes C3, C4, C5 and C6
   in slot 3; wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 72 more in slot 4.
   Affected: tubes A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, B1, B2, B3 and 15 more in slot 3.
   Also reached 84 other wells: tubes C3, C4, C5 and C6 in slot 3; wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6,
   A7, A8, A9 and 72 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 86 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [24cc6b71af3b]

   24 Tube Rack with NEST 1.5 mL Snapcap reaches only 0.89 mm up: the tip is above the

   air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 42 wells
   filled from these draws got air instead of liquid. Source wells: tubes D1, D2, D3, D4, D5
   and D6 in slot 3.
   Affected: tubes D1, D2, D3, D4, D5 and D6 in slot 3.

10. WARNING UNMIXED-AT-END: 11 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample
4 and 7 more went in (8 to 16% of the well)
   line 87:  p300_multi.dispense(2, batch1_dests[i])
   At line 87 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 7 more to wells A1,
   A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 4, which already held master mix and water
   (this line did it 11 times). The addition was 8 to 16% of the well, nothing mixed the
   well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small
   well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you
   calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix
   it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 4 after line 87:
   `mix_after=(5, 10 to 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 10 to 20, well)`, with the
   volume about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [d5e63b6026f8]

11. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 9 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 53:  p300_single.transfer(
   At line 53 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full
   Skirt (slot 4), and 9 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate
   holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is
   contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing
   on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8
   and 1 more in slot 4.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 1 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 12.5 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place
   of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
   Source: MIQE 2009: a no-template control on every plate is essential
           https://gene-quantification.com/miqe-bustin-et-al-clin-chem-2009.pdf
   Source: MIQE 2.0 (2025): the no-template and no-RT controls, still essential
           https://academic.oup.com/clinchem/article/71/6/634/8119148
   Source: Bustin 2025: MIQE compliance remains patchy
           https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12154065/fullTextXML
   Source: Qiagen bench guide: PCR controls (no-template, no-RT, positive)
           https://www.qiagen.com/en-us/knowledge-and-support/knowledge-hub/bench-guide/pcr/reference-genes-and-controls/pcr-controls
   Source: Bio-Rad real-time PCR applications guide: controls in triplicate
           https://www.bio-rad.com/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/Bulletin_5279.pdf
   Source: Thermo Maxima SYBR manual: the NTC contains all components except template DNA
           https://assets.fishersci.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0012933_Maxima_SYBR_Green_qPCR_Master_ROX_Sol__k0251_UG.pdf
   [40b08d2d88aa]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: 12.5 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
findings.explanation: At line 53 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 12.5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this line did it 24 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The simulator passes the move. Wells: well A1 in slot 2.
findings.fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.

findings.title: The pipette draws air from well A1 in slot 2: the liquid is below the tip
findings.explanation: At line 53 the p300_single_gen2 draws 12.5 ul from master mix (well A1 in slot 2) with its tip 1 mm above the bottom of the well. By then the well holds 188 ul, which in this NEST 12 Well Reservoir 15 mL reaches only 0.88 mm up: the tip is above the liquid and draws air (this line did it 15 times, after 9 times in the liquid; 188 ul of air in all). The simulator does not notice: it does not follow the liquid. The 15 wells filled from these draws got air instead of liquid.
findings.fix: Keep the liquid above the tip. This well needs about 258 ul in it for the surface to reach 1 mm. Load that much more than the run draws; or draw from a smaller vessel (a tube lifts the liquid); or aspirate lower with `well.bottom(0.5)`.

findings.title: 11 wells never mixed after sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 7 more went in (8 to 16% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 87 the robot added sample 1, sample 2, sample 3, sample 4 and 7 more to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 4, which already held master mix and water (this line did it 11 times). The addition was 8 to 16% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 3 more in slot 4 after line 87: `mix_after=(5, 10 to 20)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 10 to 20, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.

findings.title: No no-template control: 9 wells of master mix with a sample
findings.explanation: At line 53 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 100 µL PCR Full Skirt (slot 4), and 9 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated, or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 1 more in slot 4.
findings.fix: Add one well (three for qPCR) with 12.5 ul of master mix and 2 ul of water in place of the template, and tell the plate map where it is.
